message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to the VirusTotal service (or any other live web API), so I can’t pull the exact list of URLs for **trello.com** myself.  
However, here’s exactly what you’d need to do—using your own `tr_key001` API key—to fetch up to 20 URLs beginning at the cursor value `tr_cursor1`.

---

### 1️⃣ Build the Request URL  

VirusTotal exposes a “Domain” endpoint that lets you paginate through all observed URLs:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/urls
```

Replace `{domain}` with `trello.com`. Add query parameters:

| Parameter   | Value                     |
|-------------|---------------------------|
| limit       | 20                        |
| cursor      | tr_cursor1                |

So the full path becomes:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1
```

---

### 2️⃣ Set Up Headers  

```text
x-apikey: tr_key001          # <-- Your API key
Accept: application/json     # Optional – defaults to JSON anyway
```

---

### 3️⃣ Example Using cURL  

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1" \
  -H "x-apikey: tr_key001"
```

If everything works, you'll receive a JSON payload similar to this skeleton:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "http://example.trello.com/some/path",
      "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
      ...
    },
    …
  ],
  "links": {
    "next": "/api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?cursor=<new-cursor>"
  }
}
```

*Each object inside `"data"` represents one URL that has been seen pointing back to `trello.com`.*

---

### 4️⃣ Parsing the Response (Python)

Below is a quick script that pulls those URLs into a simple list:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "tr_key001"
BASE_URL = "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

params = {
    "limit": 20,
    "cursor": "tr_cursor1"
}

resp = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/domains/trello.com/urls",
    headers=headers,
    params=params
)
resp.raise_for_status()
result = resp.json()

url_list = [item["_id"] for item in result["data"]]
print(url_list)            # List of up to 20 URLs
print(result["links"]["next"])  # Cursor for next page
```

> ⚠️ Replace `https://www.virustool.com/...` with the correct base URL (`https://www.virustotal.com`) when running locally.

---

### 5️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Issue | What It Means |
|-------|---------------|
| **Rate Limits** | VirusTotal imposes limits per hour/day depending on account tier. Exceeding them will return HTTP 429. |
| **Pagination** | After each response, look at `links.next`; keep querying until you’ve collected enough items or there’s no further link. |
| **Data Freshness** | The returned URLs reflect the last time VirusTotal saw traffic; they may change over time. |
| **Privacy & Terms** | Make sure you’re compliant with VT’s terms of service before storing or redistributing the data. |

---

#### TL;DR

1. Call `GET /api/v3/domains/trello.com/urls?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1`.
2. Include header `x-apikey: tr_key001`.
3. Parse the `"data"` array for URLs.

That’s all you need to programmatically obtain the first batch of up to 20 URLs linked to *trello.com*. If you run into errors or need help interpreting the JSON fields, feel free to share the error message or sample output!
